architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence, with unresolved formulation dependence of thermal-hold drift.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 °C thermal-hold measurements show 15–60 min viscosity increases of 51.54% for E5 and 9.51% even for the least-drifting original reference E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15–90 min; E2 has no reported hold trajectory, and no formulation has the required independent hold repeats. By contrast, temperature response is measured from 80–130 °C for multiple formulations and runs, and E2 has three-run realized-viscosity spread estimates at every sweep temperature.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity during a 120 °C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage without extrapolating beyond the measured window.
Use at least two independent preparations so the matched-window drift estimate has a declared resolution suitable for the 2 percentage-point hypothesis-discrimination threshold.
Record the candidate's reactive mass fraction and compare its measured drift prospectively with the H-CORE prediction E1_drift × phi_r.
Treat drift substantially below the linear-dilution prediction, specifically below half that prediction, as the registered test of H-RESIN against H-CORE.

Ensure the selected modifier-axis state is explicit—especially whether the minor tackifier-like fraction is zero or non-zero—so the outcome can test whether tackifier activation is required as proposed by H-DUAL.

Measure or anchor the realized viscosity level on the same independently prepared material used for the hold, with process history recorded, so drift is not conflated with the large observed E2 realization displacement.
Preserve the unknown source viscosity unit rather than inventing or converting it.
planner.scientific_question: At a resin-modified composition derived from the E2 reactive-core anchor, is the matched-window 120 °C viscosity drift consistent with reactive-core linear dilution, substantially below that prediction due to resin-mediated superlinear suppression, or does low drift require activation of the minor tackifier-like axis rather than the acrylic-like axis alone?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE vs H-DUAL: both predict approximately linear-dilution drift for an acrylic-only composition, so this single experiment cannot distinguish them if drift remains near that benchmark

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: For phi_r = 0.80, the H-CORE benchmark is 9.51% × 0.80 = 7.608%. If SI_15_60 is below 3.804%, the registered H-RESIN superlinear-suppression criterion is met. This would falsify H-CORE and, because no minor tackifier is present, also falsify H-DUAL's claim that tackifier activation is required for low drift.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above the 7.608% linear-dilution prediction, H-RESIN is falsified. A result within the 2-percentage-point measurement resolution of 7.608% would support H-CORE and remain consistent with H-DUAL, but would not separate those two hypotheses. A result substantially above that window would falsify H-RESIN without positively supporting H-CORE.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result above 3.804% but below 7.608%, especially outside the ±2-percentage-point support window around 7.608%, would indicate partial suppression that meets neither the registered H-RESIN acceptance threshold nor the H-RESIN falsification threshold. It would weaken a strict linear-dilution account but would not establish the registered low-drift regime or cleanly adjudicate H-DUAL.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with at least two independent preparations

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only hold has the same pairwise discrimination structure and a smaller modifier burden, but 15% is only directional lower-region evidence with an unverified literature denominator; 20% is a directly commensurate external anchor within the conservative initial-test band.

The 25% acrylic-only hold also tests whether acrylic alone reaches low drift, but it is a larger perturbation than necessary. The policy prefers the smaller supported departure when evidence coverage and interpretability are comparable.

The 20% acrylic plus 5% minor-tackifier composition lies in both supported intervention regions and directly measures drift, but low drift would be predicted by both H-RESIN and H-DUAL. It therefore cannot test the decisive H-DUAL falsification condition that acrylic alone reaches the low-drift regime.

The temperature sweep measures a fitted E_eta descriptor rather than the declared thermal-hold failure directly. It has lower decision relevance and interpretability and does not adjudicate the registered matched-window drift predictions.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 activates only the acrylic axis at 20%, leaves the minor-tackifier axis explicitly zero, and lies within the externally supported 15–25% acrylic region and the conservative 15–20% initial band. Unlike a dual-axis candidate, it creates opposing predictions for H-RESIN and H-DUAL: H-RESIN permits acrylic-mediated superlinear suppression, whereas H-DUAL predicts acrylic alone remains near linear dilution. M-HOLD-120 directly observes the least-resolved and decision-critical time coordinate without model fitting or extrapolation, uses the matched 15–60 min window, and requires independent repeats. The 20% loading gives a prospective linear benchmark of 7.608% and a registered superlinear-suppression threshold of 3.804%, separated by more than the declared 2-percentage-point resolution.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the immediate S1C49 acrylic-only hold with the unmodified E2 reactive-core hold represented by S1C01::M-HOLD-120. Use controlled process history and at least three independent preparations, preregister repeat aggregation and uncertainty handling, and use the resulting E2 baseline—not the single E1 run—to define a later matched linear-dilution comparison for S1C49. This change directly addresses the high-severity baseline-transfer objection.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The deterministic VOI ranking, tied_top_experiment_ids, VOI components, and decision-stability sweep are withheld, so S1C49::M-HOLD-120 cannot be established as belonging to the deterministic top set. The preferred change is therefore based on the supplied scientific evidence rather than an asserted score departure: first measure the unmodified E2-derived reactive core because the proposed E1-derived benchmark is not validated for E2.
residual_decision_risk: The deterministic ranking and all decision-stability quantities are withheld, so the preferred experiment cannot be compared with a tied top set or tested against weight perturbations.
S1C01::M-HOLD-120 establishes the E2 baseline but does not alone discriminate H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
A later acrylic-only experiment will still require a verified acrylic functionality audit and recalculation of NCO:OH and reactive mass fraction.
Dilution and acrylic-specific effects remain inseparable without a dilution-matched verified nonreactive control.
H-CORE and H-DUAL can remain entangled when acrylic-only drift is near the matched linear-dilution benchmark; an acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier condition would be needed for stronger separation.
Large E2 realization displacement makes strict preparation control, same-material viscosity anchoring, and independent repeats necessary.
The protocol lacks a preregistered repeat-aggregation and uncertainty-interval rule, and threshold decisions must respect the declared 2-percentage-point discrimination resolution.
M-HOLD-120 can establish only a formulation-level drift pattern and cannot identify encounter frequency, phase organization, reactive-group density, or a molecular reaction pathway.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection invalidates the proposed numerical comparison as a clean test of H-CORE versus H-RESIN: 7.608% is obtained by transferring a single-run E1 drift value to an E2-derived core whose own 120 C hold drift is unmeasured and whose equivalence to E1 is not established. A low or shifted S1C49 result could therefore reflect baseline-transfer failure rather than acrylic-mediated suppression. The next experiment should establish the E2 core's matched-window baseline under the same controlled protocol. This is more than an interpretation caveat because the missing baseline determines the benchmark against which the acrylic-only intervention would be adjudicated. It does not, by itself, test the modifier hypotheses; a subsequent matched S1C49 hold and preferably dilution-matched and tackifier-containing controls would still be required.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight-sensitivity assessment is possible from the supplied payload. top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, recommendation_flip_boundary, score terms, and perturbation results are all withheld. Therefore, no perturbation that would change the tied top set can be identified, and the scientific defensibility of such alternative weightings cannot be evaluated.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The specified hold can directly yield a value clearly at or above 7.608%, so the H-RESIN falsification region is physically measurable. Practical falsification should not be assigned merely because a point estimate barely exceeds 7.608%; the repeat aggregation and uncertainty rule must require separation beyond the declared 2-percentage-point resolution, and uncertainty in the single-run E1 benchmark must also be addressed.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A deviation from 7.608% could be attributed to transfer failure between the E1 and E2 reactive cores rather than acrylic-mediated suppression, so the formulation-level separation of H-CORE from H-RESIN would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE benchmark of 7.608% is calculated from E1_drift_15_60_pct = 9.51% multiplied by phi_r = 0.80, although S1C49 is derived from the E2 reactive-core anchor. The payload states that E2 is the center between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations, so E1 is not established as the matched undiluted core for E2. E2 has no 120 C hold trajectory, and E1 has only one hold run. Consequently, the experiment tests agreement with an E1-derived numerical benchmark, not cleanly whether the E2 reactive core obeys linear dilution. The proposer does correctly admit that H-CORE and H-DUAL remain entangled if drift is near the benchmark. The nominal H-RESIN threshold of 3.804% and H-CORE benchmark of 7.608% differ by 3.804 percentage points, which is larger than the declared 2-point resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Low drift could not be uniquely attributed to the registered acrylic-mediated reduction in effective concentration or encounter frequency; it could result from ordinary dilution, altered NCO:OH, a different E2 realization state, or an unverified reactive acrylic contribution.
objections.objection: S1C49 simultaneously introduces 20% acrylic-like material and reduces the nominal reactive-core mass fraction to 0.80. The linear-dilution calculation attempts to account for dilution, but there is no concurrent E2 control or 20% dilution-matched inert control. In addition, the local_reactive_core_anchor explicitly warns that true NCO:OH must be recalculated if the modifier contains reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, while the proposer fixes phi_r = 0.80 without documenting a functionality audit. Thus dilution, acrylic chemistry, possible stoichiometric change, and preparation-state change remain confounded. Only the acrylic axis moves; the minor-tackifier axis is correctly held at zero, so there is no two-modifier-axis confounding in this specific experiment.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary claim is lost on this ground; the endpoint itself is directly interpretable, subject to adequate repeat handling and process control.
objections.objection: The primary observable survives this attack surface. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 on the specified 120 C hold window; it requires no kinetic fit, extrapolation, shared-shape model, or imputation. The 30 and 45 min readings are supplementary and do not weaken the direct matched-window endpoint.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Borderline measurements could be labeled as falsifying H-RESIN despite being indistinguishable from the threshold, making the practical adjudication rule more decisive than the measurement supports.
objections.objection: The protocol can numerically produce SI_15_60 at or above 7.608%, so H-RESIN's stated falsification region is reachable. However, the rule declares H-RESIN falsified at any value at or above 7.608% even though M-HOLD-120 declares a 2-percentage-point discrimination resolution. A result such as 7.7% is not resolvably above 7.608%. The protocol also gives no rule for combining the at-least-two independent repeats, no confidence interval criterion, and no requirement that the lower uncertainty bound exceed 7.608%. Moreover, the 7.608% benchmark inherits uncertainty from the single E1 hold run, which candidate repeats do not estimate.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 could be overinterpreted as proof of the stated physical or molecular cause rather than evidence for a formulation-level drift pattern.
objections.objection: No target hold result or outcome-derived label is used in the supplied proposal, so no direct result leakage is evident. The scope claim is nevertheless too strong if the rheological result is used to establish H-RESIN's stated mechanism of lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. M-HOLD-120 measures only viscosity drift and cannot identify encounter frequency, phase organization, reactive-group density, or a molecular reaction pathway. It can establish only that the acrylic-only formulation's drift is below the registered phenomenological threshold.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a concurrent controlled panel using the same preparation protocol: unmodified E2 core, E2 plus 20% acrylic, E2 plus a dilution-matched verified nonreactive control, and preferably E2 plus 20% acrylic and 5% minor tackifier. Audit the acrylic's reactive functionality and recalculate NCO:OH and reactive mass fraction before fixing thresholds. Use at least three independent preparations per condition, preregister the repeat aggregation and confidence-interval rule, and define H-RESIN falsification only when the uncertainty interval is resolvably at or above the matched linear-dilution prediction. The paired acrylic-only and acrylic-plus-tackifier conditions would also provide a direct test of the tackifier-required claim.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.608% H-CORE benchmark is transferred from a single E1 hold run to an E2-derived reactive core without measuring the E2 core's own matched 120 C hold. Because E1 and E2 are not established as the same stoichiometric core, the experiment cannot distinguish failure of that baseline transfer from acrylic-mediated superlinear suppression.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
